exercises.name: Barbell back squat
exercises.description: Primary lower-body strength lift for leg drive and total-body force.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.description: Primary horizontal press for upper-body strength.

exercises.name: Trap-bar deadlift
exercises.description: Primary hinge for posterior-chain strength and powerful leg drive.

exercises.name: Barbell overhead press
exercises.description: Simple vertical press for shoulder and upper-body strength.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.description: Heavy horizontal pull for upper-back strength with minimal lower-back fatigue.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.description: Simple vertical pull for lats and upper-back strength.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian split squat
exercises.description: Single-leg strength for hips, quads and stability.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.description: Simple posterior-chain accessory for hamstrings and glutes.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrugs
exercises.description: Simple trap and upper-back strength work.

workouts.name: Full Body A - Squat & Bench
workouts.description: Build the two main prop strength qualities first: strong leg drive and strong horizontal pressing, with simple upper-back work.

exercises.notes: RPE 7-8. On the Monday after a match use RPE 6-7 and only 2 working sets if legs are still beaten up.

workouts.name: Full Body B - Deadlift & Press
workouts.description: Build posterior-chain strength, overhead strength and single-leg robustness without complicated exercises.

exercises.notes: RPE 7-8. Powerful clean reps; no grinders.
Controlled reps; do not chase soreness.

workouts.name: Full Body C - Secondary Strength
workouts.description: Add a third simple strength exposure on non-match weeks without leaving the legs exhausted for Saturday speed work.

exercises.notes: Moderate load; controlled hinge. Keep 2 reps in reserve.

parts.detail: Complete the club rugby training session as coached.

conditioning.howToUse: Treat this as a hard sport session. Do not add separate conditioning afterwards.

conditioning.name: Rugby Match
conditioning.purpose: Competitive match exposure and the highest-priority rugby conditioning of the week.

parts.name: Match
parts.detail: Warm up with the team and play the scheduled fixture.

conditioning.howToUse: Match performance takes priority over optional conditioning and Friday strength.

conditioning.name: Speed Saturday
conditioning.purpose: Develop prop-relevant 10-30 m acceleration with full recovery and no equipment.

parts.name: Build-up
parts.detail: 5 min easy movement, then 3 progressive 20 m runs from roughly 60% to 80%.

parts.name: 10 m accelerations
parts.detail: 6 x 10 m from a standing start. Walk back and take extra rest if needed.

parts.name: 20 m accelerations
parts.detail: 4 x 20 m at 90-95% effort with full walk-back recovery.

parts.name: 30 m accelerations
parts.detail: 2 x 30 m smooth fast running with full recovery.

conditioning.howToUse: Speed quality matters more than fatigue. Stop if acceleration clearly slows or mechanics deteriorate.

conditioning.name: Prop Fitness Saturday
conditioning.purpose: Combine a small amount of acceleration work with repeat-effort rugby conditioning using only a field.

parts.name: Build-up
parts.detail: 5 min easy movement, then 3 progressive 20 m runs.

parts.name: Acceleration
parts.detail: 4 x 15 m at 90-95% with full walk-back recovery.

parts.name: Repeat-effort shuttles
parts.detail: 10 m out/back + 20 m out/back, then 60 sec walking rest.

parts.name: Conditioning finish
parts.detail: 20 sec hard shuttle running, then 40 sec walk.

conditioning.howToUse: Keep the first sprint section fast and fully recovered. The shuttles provide the fatigue; do not turn the speed work into conditioning.

conditioning.name: Low-Load Saturday
conditioning.purpose: Keep a small sprint exposure while reducing total load between harder weeks.

parts.name: Build-up
parts.detail: 5 min easy movement.

parts.name: Acceleration microdose
parts.detail: 4 x 10 m relaxed-fast accelerations with full walk-back recovery.

parts.name: Easy aerobic work
parts.detail: 15-20 min very easy jog/walk around the park at conversational effort.

conditioning.howToUse: This should feel easy overall. The accelerations are crisp but low volume; the aerobic work is recovery-level.

conditioning.name: Pre-Match Rugby Primer
conditioning.purpose: Prime acceleration and movement quality before a rugby match without creating meaningful fatigue.

parts.name: Build-up
parts.detail: 5 min easy movement, gradually building intensity. Finish with 3 progressive 20 m runs at approximately 60%, 70% and 80% effort.

parts.name: Acceleration
parts.detail: 10-15 m acceleration at approximately 85-90% effort. Walk back and fully recover before the next repetition.

parts.name: Sharp finish
parts.detail: 2 x 20 m smooth fast runs at approximately 85% effort with 90 sec recovery. Stay relaxed and finish feeling fresh.

parts.name: Walk-off
parts.detail: 2-3 min easy walking.

conditioning.howToUse: Use on the Friday before a Saturday match only when you feel reasonably fresh. This is a primer, not a fitness session. Keep every effort smooth and submaximal. If Thursday rugby was unusually hard, sleep has been poor or the legs feel heavy, skip this session and rest instead.

conditioning.name: Monday Easy Treadmill Maintenance
conditioning.purpose: Maintain aerobic fitness and running frequency without creating significant fatigue for the rest of the rugby training week.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 0.5-1.0% incline. Walk 3 min @ 4.5 km/h, then 3 min @ 5.2-5.5 km/h.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run continuously for 20 min at an easy conversational effort, approximately RPE 5-6. Use roughly 7.5-8.0 km/h once comfortable with continuous running.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 4 min @ 4.0-5.0 km/h.

conditioning.howToUse: Use as an easy Monday aerobic run alongside the main Wednesday treadmill session. Keep it deliberately comfortable and do not progress it aggressively. After a Saturday match, reduce the pace or duration if the legs are still heavy, and skip it entirely if you are particularly sore.
